messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: p99 streaming latency exceeded SLO on canary-v13 (route: /v1/stream/generate). p99 ~ 12.6s, p95 ~ 1.9s, error rate up to 2%. Alerting on-call.
Alice Kim: ack. taking primary. pulling graphs now — linking dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/streaming/canary-v13
Alice Kim: quick summary: canary-v13 rolled ~35m ago, traffic 10% via traffic-shipper, spike started ~5m ago. streaming tail jumps.
Ben Ortiz: I'm paged, en route. Any customer hits?
Mike Lopez: customer TextFlow reported elevated latencies and some streaming timeouts (~3 failures in last 10m). CS is on a call.
Casey Nguyen: data point: mux queues on canary hosts spiking, backlog depth x3. Looks like request serialization for streaming multiplexing is stalling.
Priya Shah: perf note: observed repeated KV-cache misses on prefix cache during canary. Could be model kv layout change causing cache thrash.
Alice Kim: ok. initial hypothesis: new model variant (v13) changed KV access pattern -> increased memory paging -> mux stalls -> p99 tail. Plan: short-circuit canary traffic to baseline v12 while we triage.
Ben Ortiz: agree. who can execute traffic-shift? I can run a quick routing tweak. Casey, can v12 accept full 10% back?
Casey Nguyen: v12 has headroom. We'll shift the 10% off canary to v12. Doing canary traffic down to 0% via router-ctrl.
deploy-bot: Running route update: set-weight canary-v13=0, baseline-v12=10
deploy-bot: OK — rollout completed (propagated to edge routers).
Alice Kim: monitoring now. p99 dropping?
Priya Shah: initial metrics show p99 for stream route dropped from 12.6s -> 1.4s over the next 45s. error rate trending down. :thumbsup:
Ben Ortiz: nice. leaving canary instances isolated for debugging. Do not terminate pods yet.
Casey Nguyen: grabbing heap/kv stats from canary host nodes. attaching snippet of top offending logs:
```
[2026-03-15T08:42:11Z] mux: waiting on kv-fetch for prefix 'session-uid-...' (latency 320ms)
[2026-03-15T08:42:11Z] kv-cache: miss -> fallback to model store (read 1.2s)
[2026-03-15T08:42:12Z] io: write stall, epoll wake delay 4000ms
```
Casey Nguyen: also seeing increased page faults and occassional OOM-kernel reclaim activity on canary GPUs (small but visible).
Mike Lopez: Customer impact: TextFlow experiencing higher perceived latency during the window; they want postmortem. CS asked if we can confirm root cause before official statement.
Alice Kim: action items: (1) preserve canary nodes for forensic (no restart), (2) collect full kv-cache traces and model memory access patterns, (3) check quantization/embedding table changes in v13 model weights, (4) run a controlled replay against canary with higher qps to reproduce. Ben, Casey you handle infra/model artifacts. Priya + I will coordinate customer comms.
Ben Ortiz: capturing node dumps and kernel metrics now. command run: `ssh root@canary-host-07 'sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 30'` then scp.
Casey Nguyen: running a synthetic streaming load against canary with same input distribution. Reproduced p99 ~ 11s locally. KV-access hot path shows different key lengths -> more lookups per token.
Priya Shah: interesting — v13 tokenizer packs longer prefix contexts which cause more KV hits per token. Combined with weaker prefix caching policy in runtime, thrash occurs under multiplexed streams.
Alice Kim: notes: root cause likely model change (access pattern) minus a runtime cache-policy mismatch. Mitigation: rollout rollback (we already drained traffic), and permanent fix options: tune prefix cache policy, adjust model's KV layout, or reduce canary traffic for longer soak.
Ben Ortiz: oncall handoff: I'm primary for live mitigation until 09:30 UTC. Paging silence set for the group.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Ben Ortiz.
Casey Nguyen: I will create a follow-up PR to change cache eviction threshold and add telemetry on key-length distribution.
Alice Kim: documenting customer impact: outages ephemeral, p99 spike window ~ 08:37–08:43 UTC, affected traffic slice 10% canary, ~0.6% of global streaming requests experienced >5s addl latency, TextFlow saw 3 timeouts.
Mike Lopez: I'll draft a customer note stating we rolled back canary and are investigating root cause; will request permission to share timeline after postmortem.
Priya Shah: postmortem owners: Casey (tech root cause), Ben (oncall timeline/mitigation), Alice (customer comms). I'll add regression tests for future canary model KV access pattern changes.
Alice Kim: final status: canary traffic 0%, baseline stable, metrics returned to SLOs. preserving artifacts for postmortem. Closing the live page once Ben confirms all logs captured.
Ben Ortiz: logs and perf traces saved to s3://redwood-incident/4332100000/; I verified core artifacts. handback to oncall rotation (next oncall: Jordan Li).
Alice Kim: thanks team. launching postmortem doc and linking here once created. :white_check_mark:
